anomalies.observed: Both isolated CAN transceivers have their isolated-side ground pins tied to the same board ground: U10.4(GND1), U10.5(GND2), U11.4(GND1), and U11.5(GND2) are all on the GND net.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the CAN interfaces as isolated buses implemented through isolated CAN transceivers. For that architecture to be valid, GND1 and GND2 of each isolated transceiver must be separate ground domains, not shorted together.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The CAN bus side is not galvanically isolated from the CM4/compute side. The board would behave as a non-isolated CAN interface, losing the intended isolation and increasing susceptibility to ground loops and common-mode disturbances.

parsed.summary: The design files deviate from the specified isolated CAN architecture: the isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have GND1 and GND2 shorted to the common GND net, defeating the intended isolation.
